content:
Tara: Quick sync — need to lock onboarding gates for Q3 catalog intake. Main tradeoff: speed-to-serve vs cost vs customer stability. Can we agree on launch criteria and migration/rollback windows?
Sam: Do we have a baseline for pass/fail on the eval suite? Last I checked we used 95% pass on sample prompts.
Jia: 95% is a hard bar for some of the smaller open families. Suggest a 90% automated threshold + a mandatory qualitative review for edge-case NLU tasks.
Alex: From sales: customers expect parity with their pinned baseline. Any behavior that degrades customer UX must be opt-in. A couple enterprise customers already asked for pin exceptions.
Kevin: Agree with opt-in path. Also want a clear migration window and rollback promise — customers want 30 days and export tooling for audit.
Tara: Proposed launch criteria (draft): cost <=1.5x baseline, latency p50 <=200ms, quality >=90% on eval suite A. Migration: 30d opt-in window + rollback path. Does that feel reasonable?
Sam: Latency p50=200ms is tight on 8-bit quant variants at seq len 1024 on current infra. Could we accept p50=250ms, and p95=500ms?
Marco: Ops perspective: 250/500 is much more reliable with our autoscaling settings. Need a circuit breaker: if model p95 >1s for >5min, auto-fallback to pinned baseline.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled for tomorrow 06:00 UTC — eng-oncall notified :rocket:
Jia: For benchmarks, we should split evals: NLU eval set + codegen eval set. Codegen needs different metrics (pass@k / BLEU-like) and can tolerate slightly higher cost.
Linda: Legal ask: onboarding checklist must include data residency flags and KMS/HSM configuration for Private deployments. Export control notes required for certain partners.
Alex: Sales can offer early access cohort: Acme and DataCorp are willing to sign opt-in clauses and pay a delta for pinned exceptions.
Tara: Action items: 1) Sam — draft fallback/runbook + autoscale knobs (due Fri). 2) Jia — curate eval subsets + per-task thresholds (due Wed). 3) Kevin — draft migration comms + opt-in docs (due Thu). I'll own the final gating doc and rollout checklist. Any objections?
Kevin: Small correction — my name is Kevin :) No objections otherwise.
Sam: No objections. Quick question on billing: if we allow pin exceptions, do we bill at baseline rate or model-specific cost?
Alex: Sales preference: bill at model-specific rate; customers requesting legacy pins pay the delta.
Tara: We'll need product + finance signoff on that model. I'll ping Finance and share a PRD.
Jia: One more request: add a continuous quality-regression monitor tied to the prompt set. If quality drops by >3% vs baseline, throttle traffic and trigger rollback.
Marco: Confirmed — SRE can wire the monitor into the circuit breaker flow. Need concrete thresholds in the runbook.
Tara: Great. I'll update the rollout checklist with: eval thresholds per-task, latency/cost SLOs, circuit breaker rules, migration comms, and legal flags. Thanks everyone.
Alex: Lmk if you want me to loop in Account Execs for Acme/DataCorp.
Tara: Please do. I'll attach the draft gating doc once Sam and Jia upload their pieces.
Sam: uploading runbook draft to the product folder after noon.
Jia: uploading eval subsets by EOD Wednesday.
Linda: I'll review the PRD for legal flags once it's posted.
Tara: End of thread — will follow up with the PRD link and a short checklist. :white_check_mark:
